name: Tycoons, Trusts and Trademarks
description: The merchants, bankers, inventors and founders who built the world's great fortunes and brands, from Renaissance Florence to Silicon Valley and China.

checkpoints.name: Merchant princes
checkpoints.note: The Medici Bank and Jakob Fugger lend to popes and kings, while the English and Dutch East India Companies pool money from many investors to trade across the oceans.

checkpoints.name: Banks and forges
checkpoints.note: The Rothschilds and Barings make fortunes in finance, Krupp and Siemens build steel and electrical firms, Vanderbilt turns ships and railways into wealth, and Lehman Brothers begins as a cotton trader.

checkpoints.name: The Gilded Age
checkpoints.note: Rockefeller's Standard Oil, Carnegie's steel and J. P. Morgan's banking dominate America. Jamsetji Tata, Madam C. J. Walker, Coca-Cola, De Beers and IBM show business growing across countries and industries.

checkpoints.name: The mass market
checkpoints.note: Henry Ford's assembly line puts people in cars, while Chanel, Disney, Toyota, Sony, Honda, Sam Walton's stores and Ingvar Kamprad's flat-pack furniture sell to millions.

checkpoints.name: Digital fortunes
checkpoints.note: Bill Gates, Steve Jobs, Jeff Bezos, Jack Ma and Elon Musk build companies on software and the internet, Warren Buffett shows the value of patient investing, and Ratan Tata takes an old family firm global.
